collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DEPARTURES AND EXILE (DEP-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Leaving and being left: moving huts, short journeys, visitors going home, goodbyes done well and badly, homesickness, and the rare person who sails away for good. Choosing to leave is never a rejection of one's people, and choosing to stay is never a failure.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

collection.description: A villager comes home after three days away and a friend had not noticed: say it stung, or keep it to yourself.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) has just come back from three days away gathering reeds. (subject.He/she) walks into the village expecting, maybe, a wave or two. (friend) looks up from the fire and says, "Oh, were you away?" (subject) stops. It's such a small thing. It still stings.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "Just a few days," says (subject), and goes to unpack. It bothers (subject.him/her) all evening. The next morning (child), a child, runs up and says, "You were gone! I counted! Three days!" and hugs (subject.his/her) legs. It doesn't make up for the rest of it. It does help.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: "Three days," says (subject). "I was gone three days." (friend) looks genuinely startled, then a bit ashamed. "I'm sorry. I didn't notice. That's not great." It doesn't fix the sting entirely. But (friend) asks about the trip and actually listens, and (subject) finds (subject.he/she) feels less invisible by the end of the evening.
